update.method: The four verses marked forward to M01 by later strands (Est 8:17 from the M18 x M72 pairing; Est 9:5 from M18 group C; Ecc 12:5 and Psa 103:11 from M08 group B) read in their passages (Est 8:9-9:6, Ecc 12:1-8, Psa 103:6-18) and woven by the main operation of each. Rule 77 reconciliation for fear in the touched sections: the only current claim told there (C-225, The fear of God) is unaffected; no current fear claim is untold.
update.claims_changed_note: Two new claims: dread on a people with no giver named, which brings them over (Est 8:17); fear that comes with age, under the call to remember the Creator first (Ecc 12, I read).
update.not_woven_note: None of the four left out. Est 9:5 adds only the outcome (10.10).
update.quote_note: every new quotation checked against iba.db verse (ESV)

new.text: Dread on a people is not always said to come from God: in Esther it falls with no giver named, and brings many of the peoples over to the name of those they fear
new.beyond_text: sets Est 8:17 beside the God-given dread of Gen 35:5 and the dread of Rahab and Moab, and reads its outcome as coming over, not flight or opposition

new.text: In the Preacher's picture of old age, fear comes as the body fails, with no enemy behind it, and the call is to remember the Creator before those days
new.beyond_text: reads the house and its keepers in Ecc 12:3 as the body; the passage does not explain the figure
